newsitem.title: UK: France assures Britain on truck compensation.
newsitem.headline: France assures Britain on truck compensation.

text.p: Britain said on Friday it had been reassured by undertakings given by the French government about compensation for British haulage companies whose trucks have just been released from blockades by French truck drivers.

As roadblocks across France were lifted following the settling of a bitter strike, Transport Secretary Sir George Young said Paris had told him it would consider claims for loss of earnings, deterioration of cargo and damage to vehicles.
Young said he on Friday telephoned French junior transport minister Anne-Marie Idrac about the consequences of the 12-day strike.
He released a letter he had written to Idrac following the call in which he said she had told him the claims for compensation would be dealt with speedily.
"I share your great relief that this disruption is now coming to an end, and I am reassured by the undertakings you have given me," Young told Idrac.
He said Idrac had told him British drivers seeking compensation would not need to produce statements from the French police to confirm they had been delayed.
